articles.title: Rick Springfield says he killed a man while entertaining troops during Vietnam War
articles.summary: Rick Springfield revealed on the "Joe Rogan Experience" that a mortar he fired during a Vietnam War troop visit killed someone, a moment that haunts him.
articles.body:
Rick Springfield revealed on a podcast that he accidentally killed a man while entertaining troops in Vietnam during the war.

Springfield's band traveled to Vietnam in 1968 to perform for American soldiers, where they were hired as long as they had girls in the band.

The singer fired a mortar during an attack after being told there were no friendly forces nearby, leading to the tragic realization that he had taken a life.

Long before Rick Springfield became a rock star and heartthrob, he found himself caught in the Vietnam War.

Springfield revealed he made a split-second decision that he said ended another man's life and has haunted him ever since during an appearance on the "Joe Rogan Experience" podcast. The Australian singer explained that his unlikely brush with combat began when his band traveled to Vietnam in 1968 to entertain American troops during the war.

According to Springfield, the U.S. soldiers "wanted to see, you know, girls that reminded them of home."

"So as long as we had a couple of girls in the band, they would hire you, and you could tour Vietnam during the war zone," he added. "It was pretty insane. We were there for about four months."

Springfield said he went into the experience with few expectations beyond earning a paycheck.

"It was insane. I thought, 'Oh, great. We'll make money, you know.' And, of course, we didn't make any money. We spent it all at the PX, and we weren't making much money anyway."

What began as a gig entertaining troops quickly became deadly serious when Springfield found himself caught in an attack.

"We met these guys, and we really got along well, and we stayed overnight with them, and we all got in the bunkers, in the perimeter bunkers, and I stayed in the radio shack, and we got attacked, and I'm throwing mortars down the freaking tube of the radio shack."

"It was freaky," Springfield noted. "This is before – you couldn't do any of this now."

The gravity of what happened didn't fully sink in until Springfield learned what one of his mortars had done.

"The hardest thing for me was that I had thrown a mortar down, and it had hit somebody, and they came in the next day and said, 'Hey, you got one. You got one.'"

"And that still has a hard place to land in me, you know? That's really kind of the one thing I brought back with me that I couldn't really find a place for that to land."

Springfield went on to give Rogan a more detailed account of the attack and the moments before he fired the mortar.

"It was like the movies ," he recalled. According to Springfield, the radio crackled with a warning about movement nearby before delivering a stark confirmation – there were no friendlies in the area.

"They said, 'Hey, you want to throw some mortars down the tube?' And it was John Wayne time, you know. I mean, as a young kid, I didn't really understand what I was doing."

Springfield said his youthful understanding of the moment from the Vietnam War eventually gave way to the painful reality of what he had done.

"I think it's still there, you know?" he said. "It's hard for me to kind of face that I was responsible for the end of a life, even though it's distant, and it's war," Springfield explained. "And I didn't really have anything to do with it and didn't really know what I was doing, but you know as a kid and playing, like I said, John Wayne.

"But it was... pretty heavy when I think about the reality of it."

articles.title: 10º Festival Gastronômico da Jabuticaba de Casa Branca | G1
articles.standfirst: Uma década de tradição e protagonismo da fruta. Evento vai de 11 a 15 e de 18 a 20 de setembro, na Praça da Matriz, com gastronomia, cultura, música e produtores locais.
articles.summary: Uma década de tradição e protagonismo da fruta. Evento vai de 11 a 15 e de 18 a 20 de setembro, na Praça da Matriz, com gastronomia, cultura, música e produtores locais.
articles.body:
10º Festival Gastronômico da Jabuticaba de Casa Branca — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Casa Branca (SP) se prepara para celebrar uma década de um dos principais eventos gastronômicos e turísticos do Estado de São Paulo. De 11 a 15 e de 18 a 20 de setembro, a cidade promove o 10º Festival Gastronômico da Jabuticaba, na Praça da Matriz.

Mais do que uma celebração gastronômica, o Festival evidencia a importância da jabuticaba para a identidade, o turismo e a economia de Casa Branca, reconhecida como Capital Estadual da Jabuticaba.

O município possui aproximadamente 50 mil pés de jabuticaba e cerca de 23 produtores em grande escala, além de diversos pequenos produtores. Durante o período de safra, a produção ultrapassa dois milhões de quilos da fruta, movimentando toda uma cadeia produtiva e gerando aproximadamente 1.500 empregos diretos e indiretos.

A força da cultura da jabuticaba também pode ser observada na extensão das áreas de cultivo. Considerando Casa Branca e seus distritos, são aproximadamente 300 hectares de área plantada.

A atividade representa ainda uma parcela significativa da economia local. A jabuticaba é responsável por aproximadamente 30% do faturamento do município, demonstrando a relevância da fruta não apenas como símbolo cultural, mas também como importante fonte de geração de renda e oportunidades para a população.

É nesse cenário que o Festival Gastronômico da Jabuticaba ganha ainda mais significado. Ao chegar à sua 10ª edição, o evento celebra uma tradição que une produtores, comerciantes, empreendedores, moradores e visitantes em torno de um dos maiores patrimônios de Casa Branca.

A programação reúne gastronomia, cultura, música, artesanato e produtos derivados da jabuticaba, oferecendo ao público diferentes formas de experimentar e conhecer a fruta que movimenta a economia e faz parte da história do município.

A expectativa é de que aproximadamente 100 expositores participem desta edição, fortalecendo os negócios locais e proporcionando aos visitantes uma experiência que vai muito além da gastronomia.

Ao completar 10 edições, o Festival reafirma seu papel como uma das principais vitrines de Casa Branca, promovendo o turismo, valorizando quem produz e mostrando para toda a região a dimensão da cadeia produtiva da jabuticaba.

Gastronomia, cultura, música, artesanato e produtos à base de jabuticaba.

articles.title: La IA podría ‘resucitar’ a Paul Walker en la próxima entrega de ‘Fast & Furious’: su hermano se descarta para interpretarlo
articles.standfirst: El actor falleció en 2013 en un accidente automovilístico
articles.summary: El actor falleció en 2013 en un accidente automovilístico
articles.body: La saga de películas de ‘A todo gas’ o más conocidas por su título en inglés ‘Fast & Furious’ arrancó en el año 2001, pero lo que nadie pudo prever ni imaginar es que 25 años después, la franquicia seguiría siendo rentable. Después de 10 películas, a las que añadir un ‘spin off’, las cintas protagonizadas por Vin Diesel siguen siendo apreciadas por los espectadores, sobre todo después del fallecimiento en 2013, en un trágico accidente automovilístico, de uno de los protagonistas, Paul Walker. Sin embargo, con el paso del tiempo y la llegada de las nuevas tecnologías a la industria del cine, la presencia de Walker podría ser una realidad en el próximo estreno si se cumplen las palabras que ha pronunciado su hermano Cody, en una entrevista con el medio Entertainment Weekly. Tanto Cody como su hermano Caleb ya participaron en la séptima entrega, pues fue durante el rodaje de ésta cuando Paul falleció. Sus hermanos lo sustituyeron en esa cinta para poder completar el rodaje. Ahora, 13 años después de su muerte, la figura de Paul ha vuelto a la palestra después de las palabras de su hermano en el citado medio. Y es que parece que la saga llegará a su fin con la undécima película que podría permitirse el lujo de tener a Walker en el reparto gracias a la inteligencia artificial. “Mi postura es que se haga lo que Meadow (hija de Paul) quiera ver”, indicó antes de añadir, “yo no estaría interesado en volver a hacerlo”. De hecho, su hermano alabó la forma en la que el personaje de Paul, Brian O’Connor, fue retirado de las pantallas ya que se fue para llevar una vida tranquila junto a Mia (interpretada por Jordana Brewster) y sus dos hijos. “No lo mataron, no hicieron nada cursi por el estilo, fue algo hermoso, él está criando a sus hijos. Pero si quieren hacer eso, si a Meadow le gustaría verlo, no nos necesitan ni a mí ni a Caleb”, dijo antes de referirse a la IA. “La IA no existía en 2014, así que podrían hacerlo. Hay años de material grabado que nunca se utilizó en las otras películas de 'Fast'. Son los mejores en el negocio; sabrán cómo resolverlo".

articles.title: Vuelve el calor sofocante a España durante unos días: se aproxima una ‘cresta africana’ que disparará los termómetros
articles.standfirst: Se esperan temperaturas por encima de los 40 grados en muchas localidades
articles.summary: Se esperan temperaturas por encima de los 40 grados en muchas localidades
articles.body: Las altas temperaturas están siendo la nota predominante en este verano al que todavía le quedan un par de semanas para convertirse, de manera oficial, en otoño. Muchas olas de calor y temperaturas nocturnas mucho más altas de lo normal en casi todo nuestro territorio han sido noticia durante casi tres meses. Fue el pasado miércoles, 9 de septiembre, cuando las temperaturas se rebajaron y dieron un respiro, con mínimas más propias del otoño que del final del verano. Sin embargo, tal y como apuntan los medios meteorológicos especializados, esta circunstancia se va a revertir en las próximas horas y el calor sofocante va a volver a barrer la Península Ibérica y las Islas Canarias. Tal y como indican los expertos, a partir de la mitad del fin de semana, volveremos a vivir episodios con temperaturas muy altas, principalmente por el día, ambiente estable y chubascos tormentosos muy localizados. Se espera que la jornada del domingo 13 de septiembre sea el inicio de un nuevo avance de las temperaturas en toda la Península y en las Canarias. Tanto el domingo, lunes y martes, los valores máximos del mercurio se situarán entre los 37 y los 39 grados en el valle del Guadalquivir y en las vegas del Guadiana, sin descartar que se superen los 40 en puntos muy localizados. Esas temperaturas también se podrán notar en los valles del Tajo, Ebro y Miño, así como en la depresión de Lleida e, incluso, en núcleos como Bilbao se pueden medir temperaturas superiores a los 35 grados, cifras que están entre 5 y 10 grados por encima de la media en estas fechas y más propias del mes de julio. Pero no solo serán altas las temperaturas diurnas, ya que las mínimas volverán a ser tropicales con cifras, en algunas localidades, en las que se superarán los 25 grados. Por ejemplo, zonas de Extremadura, el valle del Guadalquivir, costa mediterránea y ambos archipiélagos. De hecho, en Gran Canaria, Lanzarote y Fuerteventura se superen los 35 grados de día y durante la noche esas cifras bajen entre 7 y 10 grados y algunas localidades de las ‘afortunadas’ vivirán noches tórridas.

articles.title: Hollywood Marine veteran Rob Riggle doubts modern stars would make Jimmy Stewart's WWII sacrifice
articles.summary: Marine veteran Rob Riggle doubts today's Hollywood stars would leave fame to serve like WWII bomber pilot Jimmy Stewart, who enlisted after winning an Academy Award.
articles.body: Hollywood Marine veteran Rob Riggle has doubts about whether today's stars would be willing to step away from the spotlight to serve in uniform like WWII bomber pilot Jimmy Stewart. Stewart famously walked away from an Oscar-winning career at its peak to enlist in the U.S. Army Air Corps as a private nine months before the attack on Pearl Harbor. In the upcoming biopic "Jimmy," Riggle, who is a retired U.S. Marine officer, plays Colonel Terrill, Stewart's squadron commander and mentor. TOM HANKS PUT 'BAND OF BROTHERS' STARS IN THEIR PLACE DURING BOOT CAMP 'MUTINY', NEAL MCDONOUGH REVEALS During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 56-year-old actor and comedian weighed in on whether modern celebrities would be willing to make the same wartime sacrifice as the late movie icon. "I would be surprised if anybody made that same choice today, especially an actor of his status," Riggle said. "You got to remember, he won an Academy Award before the war," "The Hangover" star continued. "It wasn't like he was an up-and-coming actor. He was an established Academy Award-winning actor before the war. And then decided to put on the uniform and not in a safe way." "He wanted to put on the uniform and serve where he could be used best," Riggle added. "And he was a pilot, so he put his hand in the air and went into harm's way. And I don't know if you'd see that today. I mean, I hope you would, but I would be surprised." Stewart joined the military in March 1941, just 28 days after winning the best actor Academy Award for his performance in the classic 1940 film, "The Philadelphia Story." He had tried to enlist in late 1940 prior to winning his Oscar but was initially rejected for being five pounds under the weight requirement for his 6'3" frame. Determined to serve, Stewart actively gained the weight so he could reapply and enlist right after the Academy Awards. Due to his fame, the military initially tried to keep Stewart, who was a licensed commercial pilot, stateside as a flight instructor and used him for publicity and March of Dimes promotional tours. However, Stewart repeatedly requested overseas combat duty, appealing to his superiors to let him fly rather than serve in public relations. 99-YEAR-OLD WWII VETERAN AWARDED PURPLE HEART AFTER WAITING MORE THAN 80 YEARS Stewart's persistence eventually paid off, and he was sent to England in late 1943 with the 445th Bombardment Group. He went on to fly 20 official combat missions over Nazi-occupied Europe as a command pilot, squadron commander and wing commander in B-24 Liberator heavy bombers. By the end of WWII in 1945, Stewart had risen from private to full colonel. His combat awards included the Distinguished Flying Cross, the Air Medal and the French Croix de Guerre. REMEMBERING THE COLLEAGUES WE LOST: A VETERAN'S MEMORIAL DAY REFLECTION Riggle noted that people may be unaware of the danger that Stewart willingly placed himself in while serving his country. "I think Jimmy went through a lot harder service than most with the flying over Germany, dropping bombs, having to make those sorties under tremendous stress and loss of his peers," Riggle said. "But I do think when you decide to serve your country, you're kind of writing a blank check with your life and limb and I think it takes a lot to do that, so I'm so proud of the way he served his country and came back and then found a way out of the darkness of PTSD," he added. "That was pretty amazing." As a commander, Stewart carried the immense burden of sending young men into brutal anti-aircraft fire and Luftwaffe attacks. During his service, Stewart witnessed heavy losses among his men and carried deep guilt over the lives lost under his command. Biographers and historians have documented that Stewart suffered from severe psychological trauma, which caused digestive issues, insomnia, nightmares, shakes and sweats. Though Stewart's symptoms indicated that he was experiencing post-traumatic stress disorder, the formal clinical diagnosis of PTSD was not established until 1980. After returning to Hollywood, Stewart channeled his suppressed trauma into his post-war acting roles, including his performance in 1946's "It's A Wonderful Life," in which he played George Bailey, a banker who was experiencing a mental breakdown, raging at his family and contemplating suicide. GARY SINISE SAYS HIS MONEY WOULD BE ‘MOVING A LOT FASTER OUT THE DOOR’ IF HE STILL LIVED IN CALIFORNIA According to historians, portraying darker, more complex characters than in his pre-war Hollywood years enabled Stewart to process his trauma. In the years following the war, Stewart enjoyed a successful career, built a family and continued his service in the Air Force Reserve for another two decades. Stewart died from a heart attack in 1997 at the age of 89. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Riggle explained that he drew upon his own military experience in the U.S. Marine Corps while portraying Colonel Terrill. Riggle served in the Marines for 23 years, reaching the rank of lieutenant colonel and serving deployments in Af­ghanistan, Albania, Liberia and Kosovo before retiring in 2013. The actor noted that his service gave a personal understanding of what it means to send young men into harm's way. "I myself was a lieutenant colonel so I know what it is to be in charge of a group of people," he said. "I was a Marine, but I know what it's like to be responsible and in charge and I know the weight of leadership. So I felt for all the characters in the movie that have that responsibility of leading men and making decisions that could affect their lives or end their lives." Riggle launched his comedy and acting career in 1997 in New York City while he was still serving on active duty in the Marines. He had a short stint as a cast member on "Saturday Night Live" from 2004 to 2005, and later made his breakthrough as a correspondent for "The Daily Show." The actor later appeared in numerous sitcoms, including "New Girl," "Arrested Development," "The Office" and "Modern Family," in which he played Ty Burrell's character, Phil Dunphy's arch nemesis, Gil Thorpe. He has also had roles in hit movies including "The Hangover," "Step Brothers," "The Other Guys," "Dumb and Dumber To" and "Let's Be Cops." Riggle told Fox News Digital that serving in the Marines gave him the qualities and mindset that he needed to succeed in Hollywood. "Tenacity, don't quit, never give up, get up and try again," he said. "All those intangible lessons of mental toughness and fortitude, you need to have those if you're gonna be in Hollywood or any life in the arts, really." "Because people are going to reject you, people are gonna deny you, people are not gonna see it the way you see it," Riggle continued. "You've got to be able to take the blows and keep going forward. And I think that's what the Marines gave me with those intangibles." Riggle also said that his military background has helped keep fame and Hollywood success in perspective. "When you're a Marine, Uncle Sam doesn't care who you are," he said. "He still expects you to go do your job and every day get up and do it." "I think it's great," Riggle added. "I think that it's very humbling and it's a good reminder. Get up and go do your job." Riggle shared that he considers his military service to be among his top life achievements. "It's got to be right up there in the top three, next to my kids," he said. "There should be some mention of it on my tombstone, let me put it that way," Riggle added with a laugh. Riggle noted that while Hollywood is generally appreciative of former service members, he believes many civilians still harbor a fundamental misunderstanding about why men and women choose to enlist in the first place. "I have felt that Hollywood is actually very respectful toward its veterans," Riggle said. "It's been really nice to see. But if there are misconceptions out there, I think some people, again, this is a general statement, but I think people might think that people who join the military, they do it because they don't have any other choices." "And that's simply not true," he continued. "They've got a tremendous amount of choices. And they choose to serve their country." "It's an all-volunteer force," he added. "No one's making them do anything. So the people that put their hand in the air have made that decision in their mind and that decision is to serve something bigger than themselves. And I think it's quite honorable." Directed by Aaron Burns and starring "Riverdale" alum KJ Apa as Stewart, "Jimmy" follows the actor's transformative journey from Hollywood stardom to World War II combat pilot. The movie also explores his return home as a decorated Colonel who is quietly struggling with PTSD, which was then known as "combat fatigue." Tickets for the movie go on sale today. "Jimmy" depicts how Stewart was disillusioned and considering quitting acting when director Frank Capra (Max Casella) persuaded him to star as George Bailey in "It's a Wonderful Life" and how playing the role in the holiday classic enabled the actor to heal and reclaim his life. Riggle told Fox News Digital that he was drawn to the project because it's a "great American story." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE "I think it's a patriotic story," Riggle said. "I think people know Jimmy, especially younger generations, know him from his acting. I really wanted people — or I'm glad to be part of the story that's being told, about his service to his country." "I hold it to high esteem,"he continued. "So I thought his journey was fantastic, it was amazing, and it was a true American journey." "I think he's a hero," Riggle added. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS Riggle expressed his hope that audiences who watch "Jimmy" and may be unfamiliar with his military service may come to see him in a new light. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "I hope they remember the man, Jimmy Stewart," Riggle said. "Most people just remember him from 'It's a Wonderful Life.' Every Christmas they see him, and they're like, ‘Oh yeah, I love this movie.’ And there's so much more to the man." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "And I hope they remember that there are people out there — we see so much news about the bad guys," he continued. "There's a lot more stories of good guys, you're just probably not seeing enough of them. And this is a story about a really great guy who did what he thought was right, followed his heart, followed his conscience, and did what he thought he needed to do, and we're all better for it."

articles.title: Music festival planned in honour of beloved Burslem pub doorman
articles.summary: The parents of Liam Smith hope a music festival will raise awareness about epilesy.
articles.body:
The mother of a man who died following an epileptic seizure is smiling again.

It's a video of her late son that's been amusing her, although it's one that still makes her cry.

The reson for Donna Smith's mirth is that son Liam is doing karaoke on the clip. There's just one problem - he can't sing. And, she says, the footage is gettting "funnier and funnier".

It's his love of music regardless that she has found so comforting, with plans for a music festival in his memory - to raise awareness of epilepsy - described by the family as amazing.

Smith died while working as a doorman at The Old Post Office venue in Burslem, Staffordshire, last month. He was 29.

Staff said his death was a tragic loss and vowed to support the festival, due to be held on 29 August next year.

The family hopes the event - conceived by a musician who was playing the night Smith died - will become an annual occasion.

Smith was an avid music fan and regularly attended Download Festival, his parents told BBC Radio Stoke.

Donna Smith remembered of her son: "He was so funny. He'd do anything for a laugh, even if it was at his own expense.

"He couldn't sing but he got on karaoke and I've been sent a video of him singing. Even though watching it makes us cry, I've been watching it a lot more now because each time it just gets funnier and funnier."

She added: "Liam and I never knew when we were going to have a seizure, whereas some people get warning signs or they get a funny taste or can have absent seizures where they just stare at people."

The Epilepsy Foundation has described the condition as "the fourth most common neurological disorder in the world".

The idea for the festival in Liam Smith's honour came from musician Matt Swan - whose band played at The Old Post Office regularly and was playing the night Smith died.

Swan said: "He struck me as a consummate professional, he loved his music. We noticed a few times during gigs he was sort of bobbing in and out. I don't think he wanted to work that night. I think he wanted to be there with us."

articles.title: Saif Ali Khan to play Kamal Amrohi and Triptii Dimri as Meena Kumari in biopic ‘Kamal Aur Meena’ to be directed by Siddharth P Malhotra
articles.summary: Saif Ali Khan and Triptii Dimri are reportedly in advanced discussions to headline filmmaker Siddharth P Malhotra’s upcoming Meena Kumari biopic, ‘Kam.
articles.body: Saif Ali Khan and Triptii Dimri are reportedly in advanced discussions to headline filmmaker Siddharth P Malhotra’s upcoming Meena Kumari biopic, ‘Kamal Aur Meena’. According to a report by Variety India, the Netflix original will explore the lives of legendary actor Meena Kumari and filmmaker Kamal Amrohi, whose celebrated love story eventually led to marriage. The project is currently in pre-production, with discussions around contracts and shoot dates underway.Saif Ali Khan and Triptii Dimri in talks to headline ‘Kamal Aur Meena’Saif Ali Khan and Triptii Dimri could be coming together for a period drama centred on one of Hindi cinema’s most iconic couples. As per Variety India, the two actors are in advanced discussions to play the lead roles in Siddharth P Malhotra’s ‘Kamal Aur Meena’. The project is being developed as a Netflix original and is currently in the pre-production stage. According to the report, the makers are working through contractual discussions while also figuring out the actors’ shooting schedules. If the casting comes through, Saif would portray filmmaker Kamal Amrohi, while Triptii is expected to take on the challenging role of legendary actor Meena Kumari.Siddharth P Malhotra brings Meena Kumari and Kamal Amrohi’s story to screen‘Kamal Aur Meena’ will delve into the relationship between Meena Kumari and Kamal Amrohi, bringing together cinema, romance and the personal struggles that defined their lives. Meena Kumari was among the most celebrated actors of Hindi cinema, known for acclaimed performances and her distinctive screen presence. Kamal Amrohi, meanwhile, was a filmmaker and screenwriter whose work included the iconic ‘Pakeezah’, in which Meena Kumari played the lead. Their relationship developed into marriage, making their personal and professional journeys closely intertwined. The upcoming biopic is expected to focus on a defining phase of Meena Kumari’s life while also examining her bond with Amrohi.‘Kamal Aur Meena’ was announced last yearThe title ‘Kamal Aur Meena’ was announced on social media around a year ago, setting the stage for the long-gestating project. The film is being produced by Bilal Amrohi, who is the grandson of Meena Kumari and Kamal Amrohi. His involvement gives the project a direct family connection to the two central figures whose story it seeks to portray. With Siddharth P Malhotra attached to direct and Netflix backing the project, the biopic is now moving further into its development phase.Several filmmakers have previously attempted a Meena Kumari biopicMeena Kumari’s extraordinary life has attracted filmmakers for years, with several attempts being made to bring her story to the screen. Vidya Balan was previously linked to a Meena Kumari biopic backed by Pritish Nandy Communications but eventually stepped away from the project. In 2024, fashion designer-turned-filmmaker Manish Malhotra also revealed that he had decided against directing another planned biopic on the legendary actor. Kriti Sanon was reportedly attached to that version. Over the years, names including Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, Priyanka Chopra and Kiara Advani have also been associated with different attempts to tell Meena Kumari’s story.More about Saif Ali Khan and Triptii DimriOn the work front, Triptii Dimri was last seen sharing screen space with Madhuri Dixit, Dharna Durga and Ravi Kishan in 'Maa Behen'. She will be seen in Sandeep Reddy Vanga's Prabhas starrer 'Spirit'. Meanwhile, Saif Ali Khan will be seen in Priyadarshan's 'Haiwaan' alongside Akshay Kumar, slated for a release on September 11.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Vegetarian R Madhavan recalls living with family that slaughtered cows when he was a Canadian exchange student, was uncomfortable being naked during communal showers in the boys locker room: 'It was adharma for me'
articles.summary: Long before R Madhavan became an actor, he spent time in Canada as an exchange student — an experience that exposed him to a way of life vastly differ.
articles.body: Long before R Madhavan became an actor, he spent time in Canada as an exchange student — an experience that exposed him to a way of life vastly different from the one he had grown up with in India. From living with families who “slaughtered cows for a living” despite being a strict vegetarian to navigating communal showers with his basketball teammates, Madhavan has described the experience as one that played an important role in shaping him.In a conversation shared by the Indian School of Business on YouTube in 2023, Madhavan looked back at his time in Stettler, Canada, and called it “very important for my formative years”. He had travelled there as an exchange student through Rotary and found himself living in what he described as cowboy country.“I got an opportunity to be an exchange student on behalf of Rotary and I went to Canada as an exchange student. I went to a place called Stettler, which was the wild, wild west. It’s cowboy country. I lived with cowboys. I am a hardcore vegetarian but I live with families that slaughtered cows for a living so all that was ‘adharma’ for me,” he said.But it was not just the difference in lifestyle that challenged Madhavan. He also recalled an incident from his time on the local school's basketball team, which he described as the “biggest adharma” he encountered during his stay.Making it to the basketball team was a “huge achievement” for Madhavan, particularly because he was an Indian student who was not as tall as many of the other boys. However, his excitement soon gave way to anxiety when the team travelled to a neighbouring town for a seven-day tournament.“Like it happens over there, after the match, you come back to the boys locker room and you get into the shower. My ordeal started when I had to go into the shower because unlike what it is today, when you go to the men’s shower, it is just one pillar with six shower heads around it and all the boys go there like god made them and they take a shower together. It’s the most normal thing for them to do,” Madhavan recalled.For someone raised in a conservative South Indian household, the situation was completely unfamiliar. Madhavan said the thought of entering the shower was more nerve-racking than playing the basketball match itself.“I didn’t know how I was going to muster up walking there and so I decided to say, ‘To hell with it. I am going to wear my underwear and not take that off’,” he shared.His decision immediately made him stand out. While the rest of his teammates showered without clothes, Madhavan entered wearing his underwear and soon realised that his attempt to preserve his privacy had made him even more conspicuous.“When I went into the shower just wearing my underwear and the rest of them were not wearing anything, I cannot tell you how naked I felt because no one was looking at each other. They were all like, ‘What is he hiding?’ and I had to do that repetitively for seven days because the tournament was for seven days,” he said.Madhavan admitted that he initially tried to convince himself that he should simply adapt to what everyone else considered normal. By the third day, however, he realised he was better off staying true to his own comfort level.“I realised, ‘That’s not me. I am never going to be comfortable so I kept myself covered for seven days’. It was during that time that I realised that if your instincts are telling you that if you are going to be uncomfortable doing something… And for you to have the guts to actually not go with what is considered a norm, then you will have the ability to be comfortable with yourself and that was a very essential quality to get into the film industry,” he said.For Madhavan, what began as an awkward cultural adjustment eventually became a lesson in individuality. Years later, he remembered the incident not merely as an embarrassing moment, but as an experience that taught him the importance of listening to his instincts and being comfortable with standing apart from the crowd.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'If Sanjay Leela Bhansali makes a film with Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha': 'Varanasi' star Prithviraj Sukumaran reveals why he would definitely watch it on the 'first day first show'
articles.summary: Malayalam star Prithviraj Sukumaran recently opened up about the importance of choosing the right stories and understanding what connects with today’s.
articles.body: Malayalam star Prithviraj Sukumaran recently opened up about the importance of choosing the right stories and understanding what connects with today’s audiences. During a conversation with Yuvaa alongside Kareena Kapoor, the actor discussed changing audience expectations, the importance of good writing and why star power alone may not be enough to guarantee a film’s success.Prithviraj Sukumaran says he would watch Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha in a Bhansali filmDuring the discussion, the conversation turned to the kind of films that can immediately generate audience interest. Kareena Kapoor pointed out that today’s viewers are far more discerning than they are often given credit for, while Meghna Gulzar stressed the importance of actors and producers supporting writers and allowing them to explore unconventional stories. The discussion also touched upon the belief that pairing a young actor and actress is enough to make a film successful. Kareena noted that such formulas do not necessarily work with contemporary audiences, who increasingly look for strong stories and compelling narratives.Prithviraj then offered an interesting example involving acclaimed filmmaker Sanjay Leela Bhansali. He said, “If Sanjay Leela Bhansali makes a film with Amitabh Bachchan and Rekha, I will definitely watch first day first show,” with the other participants also agreeing with the sentiment.Prithviraj Sukumaran’s ‘Khalifa’ continues its theatrical runOn the work front, Prithviraj was recently seen in ‘Khalifa’, which arrived in theatres during the Onam festive season on August 20. The film has continued its theatrical run, although its box-office performance has reportedly been below expectations. According to Sacnilk, ‘Khalifa’ has recorded an India net collection of around Rs 21.41 crore, while its India gross has been reported at approximately Rs 44.63 crore. Its overseas gross is said to stand at around Rs 19.90 crore.Prithviraj Sukumaran to play Kumbha in SS Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’Prithviraj is also gearing up for one of his biggest upcoming projects, SS Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’. The globetrotting adventure stars Mahesh Babu in the lead role alongside Priyanka Chopra Jonas, with Prithviraj playing the antagonist Kumbha. The film has generated considerable anticipation, given Rajamouli’s track record of mounting large-scale cinematic spectacles and the combination of Mahesh Babu, Priyanka Chopra Jonas and Prithviraj.‘Varanasi’ is scheduled to release in theatres on April 7, 2027.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: 'Kala Hiran' makers tell Delhi HC that the film isn't ready for release as censor board certification is pending, in response Salman Khan's plea
articles.summary: The makers of 'Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legal, purportedly based on actor Salman Khan, on Thursday told the Delhi High Court that the movie is not r.
articles.body: The makers of 'Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legal, purportedly based on actor Salman Khan, on Thursday told the Delhi High Court that the movie is not ready for release as it is yet to get the censor board’s certification.The statement was made before Justice Jyoti Singh who was hearing an application by the Bollywood star seeking restraint on the release of the film. The court asked the film producer to file his response within two weeks on Salman’s plea.“The counsel appears for defendant no. 1 and on instructions states that the impugned movie at this stage is not in a releasable state as its content is yet to be certified by the censor board. Statement is taken on record. Reply be filed in two weeks, rejoinder before the next date,” the court said and listed the matter for further hearing on September 30.The court also asked the counsel for producer Amit Jani to inform it on September 14 the proposed date of release and said “till then you will not release it.”Salman Khan’s counsel said the makers were themselves saying that the movie is going to be released in September and “suppose it is released it will cause immense harm to me (Salman).”The producer’s counsel said the movie is not in a releasable form and it is yet to be sent to the censor board for certification and even the trailer has not been released.Salman Khan’s application forms part of his lawsuit on protection of his personality rights.Earlier in July, the high court had passed an interim order directing the removal of a teaser for the film and other related posts from online platforms after Salman’s objection to them. The court had said the makers of Kala Hiran cannot exploit the 59-year-old Bollywood star’s name, mannerisms and other distinctive attributes for commercial gains without his authorisation or disseminate content that injures his reputation. It had observed that using social media to disseminate content that violates personality rights or harms reputation exacerbates the mischief, given the speed, reach and permanence of digital publications.The court had restrained the makers from uploading, hosting, sharing, publicising or disseminating the teaser and other accompanying posts on any platform, including social media platforms, OTT platforms, television and print media, while directing them to take down the existing posts within 24 hours.X, Meta Platforms, Inc. and Google LLC should take down the URLs in case the uploaders do not take them down within the stipulated timeline, the court had further directed.The makers have also clarified that the movie was not Salman Khan’s biopic and he cannot invoke personality rights “to erase” the public events concerning the blackbuck controversy.Salman, in his rejoinder to the response, said he has not claimed a monopoly over any event or public discourse, and his grievance was the unauthorised commercial exploitation of his identity and other uniquely identifiable characteristics, such as his instantly recognisable bracelet, ear studs, etc., to attract viewers.In the earlier application, the actor has said the film’s poster, released on May 29, showed that there is a “blatant and obvious reference” to him. A teaser of the film was subsequently released.The plea has stated that although Salman Khan was acquitted of offences under the Arms Act by a court in Rajasthan, the main character in the poster is holding a gun, which is defamatory.“The character depicted has an uncanny resemblance to the plaintiff and is clearly seen wearing a bracelet, which is immediately and promptly identifiable with the plaintiff and no one else,” stated the application. “The poster and the proposed film are therefore clearly spreading a false narrative, misleading and appear to be completely contrary to the actual state of affairs and contrary to records,” it added.The application has also accused the filmmakers of deliberately attempting to “sensationalise” the poaching cases and making headlines to grab public attention at the cost of Salman Khan’s goodwill and reputation. Salman had earlier approached the high court for restraining various social media platforms and e-commerce websites from unauthorisedly using his name, images, persona and likeness and to protect his personality rights. The high court passed an interim order in his favour on December 11, 2025.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Kunal Kemmu reveals why he was nervous to approach Sharmila Tagore for ‘VIBE: ‘I was intimidated but once she said yes, I was excited’
articles.summary: Kunal Kemmu is gearing up for the release of his second directorial, ‘VIBE’, which also marks his first outing as a producer. In a conversation with M.
articles.body: Kunal Kemmu is gearing up for the release of his second directorial, ‘VIBE’, which also marks his first outing as a producer. In a conversation with Mid-Day, the actor-filmmaker opened up about casting his mother-in-law and veteran actor Sharmila Tagore in the film, admitting that he was initially “intimidated” to approach her. Kunal also revealed whether directing himself has changed the way he approaches his performances as an actor.Kunal Kemmu was ‘intimidated’ to ask Sharmila Tagore for ‘VIBE’Sharmila Tagore is set to return to the big screen with Kunal Kemmu’s ‘VIBE’, and the actor-filmmaker admitted that approaching his mother-in-law for the role was not easy. Speaking to the publication, Kunal revealed that he was nervous about asking Sharmila to be part of the film and was unsure about how she would react to the role.“I was intimidated to ask her, but once she said yes, I was excited to have her. I was grateful too, and I am very happy to see her in the film,” Kunal told Mid-Day.The director also explained that he wanted to present Sharmila’s character in a cinematic manner and personally approached her with the part.“I wanted to present the role in a cinematic way. I told her that I wanted her to play the part, and I'm grateful that she agreed to do it,” Kunal added.Once Sharmila gave her approval, Kunal’s initial hesitation turned into excitement about having the veteran actor on board.Sharmila Tagore returns to the big screen with ‘Vibe’With ‘VIBE’, Sharmila Tagore is set to return to Hindi cinema after a long gap. She was last seen in the 2010 Bollywood film ‘Break Ke Baad’. She later appeared in the Bengali psychological drama ‘Puratawn’ in 2025, which received critical acclaim and performed well commercially. Her inclusion in ‘VIBE’ adds another layer of interest to Kunal’s upcoming directorial, particularly given their family connection.Has directing changed Kunal Kemmu’s approach to acting?Kunal Kemmu is wearing multiple hats in ‘VIBE’. Besides directing the film, he is also leading the cast as an actor. However, the filmmaker says he does not allow his responsibilities as a director to interfere with his approach to acting. Asked by the publication whether his experience behind the camera has influenced the way he performs, Kunal explained that he keeps the two processes separate.“Actually, I don't mix acting and direction simultaneously. Film is a director's medium, and I have to deliver what the director wants. I never go to the monitor to look at my shots, because then I will be thinking if it's okay according to me or not. If the director says, ‘We got it,’ then we got it,” he said.Kunal added that he follows the same principle when directing himself, evaluating his performance in the larger context of the film rather than simply judging it from his own perspective.“So, similarly, when I am directing myself, I will go and see that performance and see if it works for everyone in the film, so my approach towards acting hasn't particularly changed,” he added.Kunal Kemmu says he has always been ‘critical’ of his performancesKunal also opened up about his tendency to critically assess his own work. However, he said that he approached his performance in ‘VIBE’ differently, choosing to trust his instincts and stay true to the character he had envisioned.“I was always critical of my performances. But in this film, I am staying true to the writer in me because I envisioned everyone doing something,” Kunal said.He further explained that his approach to acting differs from what may work for other performers.“And especially with me, because I know myself, I try to play every character as honestly as I can. Some actors have to find characters that suit their tonality and style. But when it came to me, I just let my instinct take over and hoped it would work. And if it doesn't, I'll learn from it,” he said.About Kunal Kemmu’s ‘VIBE’‘Vibe’ marks Kunal Kemmu’s return to the director’s chair after his directorial debut ‘Madgaon Express’. The upcoming film also marks his first stint as a producer. Written and directed by Kunal, ‘VIBE’ is an action-comedy featuring an ensemble cast that includes Kunal Kemmu, Preity Zinta, Sparsh Shrivastava, Dinesh Lal Yadav aka Nirahua, Yashpal Sharma and Vanshika Dhir. The film is scheduled to release in theatres on September 18.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: Henry Winkler addresses reported Tom Hanks tension after being fired from 1989 movie
articles.summary: Henry Winkler reveals he's still processing what went wrong with Tom Hanks after being fired from "Turner & Hooch" just 13 days into filming.
articles.body: Henry Winkler is opening up about the reported decades-long tension between himself and Tom Hanks, revealing he is still trying to understand what went wrong between them. In a recent interview on "In Depth With Graham Bensinger," Winkler — who was fired as director of Hanks’ 1989 movie "Turner & Hooch" after 13 days of filming — addressed the situation that initially ignited the reported rift. Winkler admitted he was not "suited" to direct the movie, but accepted the job after being handpicked by Disney executive Jeffrey Katzenberg. TOM HANKS PUT 'BAND OF BROTHERS' STARS IN THEIR PLACE DURING BOOT CAMP 'MUTINY', NEAL MCDONOUGH REVEALS "I went completely against my tummy, and it hit me in the face with a 2x4," Winkler said. "I now meet the puppies, and I meet with Tom [Hanks]... and I, at that time being insecure, I talked too much and I gave them direction. I [did] what I thought was my job, and I wanted to do it over again and apparently that p---ed them off." Winkler said the situation came to a head just 13 days into filming. SCOTT EASTWOOD SAYS HIS FATHER SENT KEVIN COSTNER HOME FROM SET WHILE FILMING 'A PERFECT WORLD' "I’m called into [Katzenberg’s] office, and he said, ‘It’s not in the dailies,’" Winkler recalled. "I then go to the set. I get my things. I drive home. I’m fired as a director... I don’t handle it well. I’m devastated." Winkler was replaced by director Roger Spottiswoode. Winkler also revealed that Hanks later declined to give permission for a clip from his "Happy Days" appearance to be used in a retrospective about the sitcom. "We did a retrospective on 'Happy Days,' and we wanted 60 seconds of Tom Hanks in his episode, and we did not get permission for that," Winkler said. Hanks appeared on the sitcom in 1982, years before his movie career took off. When asked what his "perspective" was on his relationship with Hanks, Winkler replied, "I am still working on my perspective." Asked whether he believed the relationship could ever "repair itself," Winkler responded, "Sure." 'HAPPY DAYS' STAR SCOTT BAIO SAYS HE WAS ALMOST FIRED FROM ICONIC SERIES AFTER 'GETTING A BIG HEAD' Winkler has previously spoken about the difficult experience while continuing to deny that he and Hanks had an outright feud. SCOTT EASTWOOD TOLD SHIA LABEOUF 'I'M GOING TO WHOOP YOUR A--' DURING TENSE ON-SET CLASH In comments to TMZ in 2020, which were later reported by Vanity Fair, Winkler said, "I don’t have a feud with Tom Hanks. What everybody says and what is true are two different things." Winkler added that he had seen Hanks at the Screen Actors Guild Awards that year. "It was beautiful," he said. However, during an appearance on "Watch What Happens Live" a year earlier, a viewer called in and asked the "Barry" star about the reported feud. "What was the real reason why you and Tom Hanks didn’t get along on the set of ‘Turner & Hooch,’ and did you ever wind up seeing that movie?" the fan asked. Winkler detailed his firing before discussing his relationship with Hanks’ canine co-star. "I got along great with that dog," he said. "Love that dog." Host Andy Cohen then asked Winkler if he had gone to see the movie in theaters. "I don’t even remember the title of that movie," Winkler said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Hanks has not publicly commented on the reported tension between the two actors.

articles.title: Riley Green reveals how he builds his concert setlist with fans always as the top priority
articles.summary: Riley Green revealed to Pat McAfee on Spotify how he builds every concert setlist by thinking like a working fan who saved up to buy a ticket.
articles.body: Fans are always the top priority for Riley Green. Green is a country music sensation who isn't just a hit with the OutKick audience. He's a mega-hit with millions of country music fans. The man is on a rocket ship to the top of the country music world, and it's not hard to understand why. His music spans the entire spectrum of the genre, and he cares deeply for his fans. COUNTRY STAR RILEY GREEN REVEALS WHY FAN EMOTION AT HIS SHOWS BEATS INDUSTRY AWARDS EVERY TIME It's the latter point that is incredibly important for how he crafts his career. Riley Green explains his mentality when it comes to crafting a show. Green sat down for a Spotify interview hosted by Pat McAfee, and he revealed there's one thing on his mind when crafting a setlist for a concert: COUNTRY STAR RILEY GREEN NEARLY DOVE INTO THE CROWD AFTER A FAN SPLIT HIS EAR OPEN DURING A PERFORMANCE What songs do his fans want to hear most? articles.title: Spice Girls fans feel duped after social media tease wasn’t for tour, but a music re-release
articles.summary: Spice Girls fans are telling you what they want — what they really, really want — and it’s a tour that they aren’t getting any time soon.
articles.body: Spice Girls fans are telling you what they want — what they really, really want — and it’s a tour that they aren’t getting any time soon. The disbanded girl group excited their followers on Wednesday with a social media post teasing a big announcement for the following day. A short clip posted to Instagram showed an issue of “The Stage” magazine left on a set of stairs before zooming into a clasified advertisement seeking Spice Girls Fans who are a “superfan, a collector, a music lover.” “No sheet music required but you will need a vinyl or cd player,” the ad said. Fans immediately jumped to speculation on what it could be, with many hoping for a possible reunion. “If it’s a world tour, I’m selling my house to buy tix,” one Instagram commenter wrote. Another wrote, “please say it’s @spherevegas,” referring to the popular Las Vegas venue where the Backstreet Boys are currently in residency. But some should have slowed it down and read the sign. On Thursday, the Spice Girls account announced a re-release of “all the singles” with b-sides and surprises “from the vault” on CD and vinyl. A previously unreleased demo of a song called “Do You Think About Me” was also made available on streaming services Thursday. The full collection will release in November and ranges in price from $128.99 to $380.99, according to the band’s website. The re-release is meant to honor the 30th anniversary of their single “Wannabe,” the hit that changed the trajectory of their lives. It was a blow to the ‘90s band’s most loyal fans, who were ready to promise they would be there in the stands. “Negotiating with my husband on my price cap for Spice Girls tickets today was for NOTHING,” one woman wrote in the comments. “Guys we want two things- Spice World on streaming platforms and a tour with the full line-up,” another Instagram user wrote. “Please make it happen.” “I hear the millennial sigh of devastation from across the world,” one person said. The Spice Girls have been asked repeatedly about a tour in recent years in interviews, but it appears that a reunion performance with all five original members is a pipe dream. There was a small tour across the U.K. and Ireland in 2019 that didn’t feature Victoria Beckham, aka Posh Spice. Beckham expressed her excitement to go watch her former bandmates even if she wasn’t going to be on stage. The fashion mogul has said in the last year that she hasn’t performed in years and doesn’t feel that she is the strongest singer or dancer. She told Andy Cohen on his radio show in October that she didn’t think she could even make a world tour work with the demands of her business. “Before I was in the Spice Girls, I was so self-conscious and they made me feel that I was good enough, but being on stage, I realized as fun as it is, you know, it’s not ultimately what I want to do anymore,” Beckham said. Melanie Brown, or Scary Spice as she’s known to fans, reiterated that a tour was not happening in an interview with Hello! magazine published in April. “I’m 50. You can’t be nagging everyone to go on tour if they don’t want to,” Brown said. “I laid that to rest when I turned 50.” But the women are still close friends. All but Beckham were in attendance for Melanie Chisholm’s wedding earlier this year. And though she couldn’t be there for Sporty Spice on her big day, Beckham designed the singer’s wedding dress, according to Vogue. All five women were together earlier this year, according to social media. Beckham’s youngest son posted a video on Instagram in February of the Spice Girls singing their song “Viva Forever” around a dinner table while he played guitar for him. The video has been watched more than 13 million times. “Love you all,” Beckham wrote in her son’s comment section.

articles.title: María Verdoy estalla tras la desagradable experiencia vivida al salir del gimnasio: "Empezó a tocarse sus partes delante de mí"
articles.standfirst: La presentadora fue perseguida por un desconocido
articles.summary: La presentadora fue perseguida por un desconocido
articles.body: María Verdoy, quien fuera presentadora de Mediaset durante muchos años, ha denunciado públicamente haber sido víctima de acoso sexual al salir de entrenar en el gimnasio. A través de su perfil oficial de Instagram, la periodista relató con indignación un desagradable episodio en plena calle con el fin de visibilizar conductas machistas que siguen impunes. Los hechos ocurrieron cuando un desconocido se le acercó en la calle inicialmente para pedirle dinero. Al responderle ella que no podía dárselo, el hombre comenzó a masturbarse y a tocarse sus partes íntimas delante de ella. "Hace una semana me pasó lo mismo con otro señor por la calle", comenzaba diciendo, apuntando que no es la primera vez que vive algo similar. María Verdoy intentó huir refugiándose en el interior de una tienda, pero el agresor la persiguió hasta la misma puerta del establecimiento, donde continuó mirándola fijamente mientras seguía tocándose. Finalmente, tras unos momentos de tensión, el individuo se marchó por su propio pie. "He salido de entrenar, ha salido un hombre que me ha pedido dinero y le he dicho que no. Me he justificado y le ha dado bastante igual porque lo que ha hecho a continuación ha sido decirme guapa y yo, obviamente, me he ido. Y bueno, ha empezado a tocarse sus partes delante de mí...", ha relatado la comunicadora a través de sus historias. "Me ha seguido por la calle y seguía tocándose sus partes, me he metido en una tienda y se ha venido hasta la puerta de la tienda tocándose y mirándome, y bueno, al final se ha cansado y se ha ido", añadía. A raíz de lo ocurrido, la presentadora no ha dudado en señalar que "está muy normalizado, se piensan que lo pueden hacer con total impunidad y nosotras lo sufrimos y, a veces, hasta nos da cosa compartirlo".

articles.title: ‘Nayyi Navelli’ teaser out: Yami Gautam plays mysterious bride suspected to be a daayan with ‘Tumbbad’ connection, netizens call it 'fresh and peak’
articles.summary: The makers of Yami Gautam Dhar’s upcoming film ‘Nayyi Navelli’ have unveiled its much-awaited teaser, offering the first glimpse of the fantasy family.
articles.body: The makers of Yami Gautam Dhar’s upcoming film ‘Nayyi Navelli’ have unveiled its much-awaited teaser, offering the first glimpse of the fantasy family entertainer directed by Balaji Mohan. The teaser introduces Yami in a never-seen-before avatar, leaving fans intrigued by her mysterious character.Released on Thursday, the nearly one-and-a-half-minute teaser blends fantasy, family drama, humour and action while keeping the central mystery surrounding Yami’s character under wraps. Several viewers have praised the film’s unusual premise and Yami’s striking new look, with some even drawing comparisons to the cult fantasy film ‘Tumbbad’.Yami Gautam plays a mysterious brideThe teaser introduces a family from Meerut whose seemingly ordinary life takes an unexpected turn when the brother-in-law begins suspecting that his seemingly perfect sister-in-law could actually be a daayan (witch). The mystery takes centre stage when he makes the shocking accusation: “Bhabhi daayan hai.” (Sister in law is a witch)What follows is a quirky mix of family dynamics, supernatural elements, comedy and action.Yami appears to be a traditional bride, but there is clearly more to her character than meets the eye. Her mysterious persona is also reminiscent of the film’s first-look poster, released in August, which featured the actress in a traditional saree while battling and killing monsters.Fans react to ‘Nayyi Navelli’ teaserSoon after the teaser dropped, several viewers took to social media to share their reactions. Some fans were particularly excited by the reported connection to ‘Tumbbad’, while others praised Yami for taking on another unconventional role.One user wrote, “Nayyi Navelli is connected to Tumbbad means it’s gonna be peak.”Another praised Yami’s transformation and wrote, “First time director Balaji Mohan gets big production house, this looks promising and sure shot super hit yami in new avatar.”Calling the teaser refreshing, another viewer wrote, “Okay, this is actually fresh. The teaser has a whole different vibe and I’m kinda here for it.”Another fan praised Yami’s career trajectory, writing, “Yami Gautam has really evolved - from romantic films like Junooniyat and Sanam Re to strong, diverse roles in Uri, Article 370, and Nayyi Navelli. articles.title: Billy Joel reveals he got brain surgery because he didn’t want to lose his ‘marbles’
articles.summary: Long Island troubadour Billy Joel revealed Tuesday that he underwent brain surgery because he didn’t want to lose his “marbles.”
articles.body: Long Island troubadour Billy Joel revealed Tuesday that he underwent brain surgery because he didn’t want to lose his “marbles.” Speaking on his SiriusXM channel, the 77-year-old “Piano Man” singer admitted he initially balked at going under the knife for hydrocephalus, a disorder he was diagnosed with in 2025. “I said, ‘Well, what does that entail?’” he said he asked the doctor. After being told that it involved having a surgeon “drill a hole through your skull” and “stick a shunt inside your brain,” Joel said “I didn’t want to do that.” “But then I read up on it, and I realized it can help improve your balance and can help your memory,” he said. “You know, I don’t want to lose my marbles. It’s hard to tell what’s age and what’s a condition, so I agreed to do the shunt, and I had surgery, and they implanted a shunt in my brain, and it actually improved things.” Joel did not say exactly when he had the surgery. But he was diagnosed in May 2025 with normal pressure hydrocephalus, which is a condition in which cerebrospinal fluid builds up inside of the skull and press on the brain, according to the Cleveland Clinic. The condition is often treatable and sometimes reversible. “They used to call it water on the brain,” Joel said on his radio show. Joel said he went to see the neurologist because he was feeling unsteady. “I noticed that my balance was not good,” he said. “I had this sense of being on a boat, like this rocking motion. I wasn’t steady on my feet.” Will he be returning to the stage anytime soon? Joel didn’t say on his show, and his longtime publicist did not immediately respond to an email from NBC News seeking an answer to that question. “The doctors told me this: because of my job, which is playing rock and roll music very loud, that it was giving me something like a concussion every time I did a show,” he said. Pounding out songs on the piano, he said, “was causing damage to my brain nerves, and I could be losing more brain cells the more shows I did. I realized that means I shouldn’t be doing this right now. I got to improve.” So Joel said he’s been going to physical therapy and following his doctors’ advice. “I’m doing whatever it is they tell me to do because I don’t want to lose it, you know?” he said. And he expects to make a full recovery. “I’m not going anywhere,” he said. “I’m here. I’m still here.”

articles.title: Jennifer Lawrence llega por fin a Instagram con una condición: "Si alguien dice algo negativo, me voy"
articles.standfirst: La actriz ha abierto su primera cuenta pública en Instagram, bajo el nombre @jlaw, después de años alejada de las redes sociales
articles.summary: La actriz ha abierto su primera cuenta pública en Instagram, bajo el nombre @jlaw, después de años alejada de las redes sociales
articles.body: Jennifer Lawrence ya está en Instagram. La actriz, que durante años se ha mantenido alejada de las redes sociales, ha abierto finalmente una cuenta pública en la plataforma bajo el nombre de usuario @jlaw. Su desembarco no ha podido ser más fiel a su personalidad: en su primer 'Reel' ha aprovechado para establecer las reglas de su nueva presencia digital. La principal condición es sencilla: nada de comentarios negativos. "Y si alguien dice algo negativo, voy a dejar Instagram inmediatamente", bromea Lawrence en el vídeo. Pero la actriz ha ido un paso más allá y ha advertido a sus seguidores de que ni siquiera será necesario que escriban algo desagradable para que ella lo perciba: "Si alguien piensa algo malo... lo voy a saber". Una amenaza en tono de humor que deja claro que la permanencia de Jennifer Lawrence en Instagram dependerá, al menos según sus propias palabras, del comportamiento de sus seguidores. La llegada de Jennifer Lawrence a Instagram también ha dejado una pequeña curiosidad. La actriz no ha podido utilizar el nombre más evidente, @jenniferlawrence, porque ya estaba ocupado. Ella misma lo explica en la biografía de su perfil con un escueto: "jenniferlawrence estaba tomado". Jennifer Lawrence no ha explicado públicamente qué la ha llevado a abrir ahora una cuenta en Instagram después de tantos años sin una presencia oficial en la plataforma. Sin embargo, su llegada coincide con una etapa profesional especialmente activa, con varios proyectos en el horizonte. Entre ellos destaca 'What Happens at Night', la nueva película dirigida por Martin Scorsese, en la que la actriz comparte protagonismo con Leonardo DiCaprio. El proyecto supone el reencuentro de ambos intérpretes después de 'Don’t Look Up'. La película sigue a una pareja estadounidense que viaja a un pequeño pueblo europeo cubierto de nieve para adoptar a un bebé. Lo que comienza como un viaje aparentemente normal irá adquiriendo tintes cada vez más extraños. El reparto se completa, entre otros, con Mads Mikkelsen, Patricia Clarkson y Jared Harris. Jennifer Lawrence ya ha terminado el rodaje de la película, por lo que su llegada a Instagram podría resultar especialmente oportuna de cara a la futura campaña promocional y al correspondiente tour de prensa junto a Leonardo DiCaprio. La lista de cuentas a las que sigue Jennifer Lawrence también ha despertado curiosidad. Entre sus primeros 'follows' aparecen algunos de sus compañeros y colaboradores de 'What Happens at Night', como Leonardo DiCaprio y Martin Scorsese, además de Josh Hutcherson, con quien compartió protagonismo en 'Los Juegos del Hambre'. También sigue a algunas de sus amigas y compañeras de profesión, entre ellas Dakota Johnson, Amy Schumer y Amy Poehler. Pero la actriz también ha demostrado que sabe perfectamente qué ofrece Instagram en materia de entretenimiento. Entre sus primeras cuentas seguidas están Kim, Khloé y Kourtney Kardashian, Kendall y Kylie Jenner y Kris Jenner. Tras su inesperado desembarco en Instagram, las expectativas sobre lo que Lawrence pueda compartir son altas. Sus seguidores esperan especialmente vídeos en los que la actriz muestre su habitual sentido del humor, además de fotografías de sus viajes, momentos cotidianos y reacciones a acontecimientos virales. También hay interés por los contenidos relacionados con sus próximos proyectos. Los rodajes, los camerinos, los viajes y, sobre todo, el futuro tour de prensa de 'What Happens at Night' podrían convertirse en una fuente de material especialmente atractiva para sus seguidores. Y es que la combinación de Jennifer Lawrence, Leonardo DiCaprio y Martin Scorsese promete generar más de un momento memorable delante y detrás de las cámaras. Por ahora, sin embargo, hay una prioridad para quienes quieran disfrutar de la nueva cuenta de Instagram de la actriz: no hacer enfadar a Jennifer Lawrence. Después de años esperando verla en Instagram, sus seguidores ya conocen la única condición para que @jlaw se quede: "Si alguien dice algo negativo, voy a dejar Instagram inmediatamente".
